title: Verification console
description: Inspect GuildGate action, configuration, store, and version behavior in the documentation's safe browser console.
content: Verification console This console runs an allowlisted set of documentation commands. It does not start a shell, make network requests, access the file system, or use persistent browser storage. Version commands Expected core information: Action checks Commands do not connect to a real route or Discord account. They show the control order and stable result for documented scenarios. Stores and reliability For 1.1.0, review: - ten store members - reservation-owner compare-and-set - atomic session caps - opaque audit cursors - bounded outbox claims - post-commit callback separation - bounded late settlement Realtime WebSocket and Socket.IO share the same inbound control path. SSE is a server-to-client stream with a bounded queue. CLI help summary For actual installed-package help, use a terminal: Security boundary Console input is parsed through an allowlist. It does not support: - arbitrary JavaScript - eval or dynamic functions - shell or process commands - HTTP or WebSocket connections - localStorage or sessionStorage - secret or token input Do not paste real configuration or secrets. The console is only for documentation examples.

title: Start in five minutes
description: Run the first GuildGate 1.1.1 action with memory stores and a transaction adapter.
content: Start in five minutes This setup is for development and tests. Memory stores are cleared when the process exits. First action Fastify connection: In production, replace memory stores with durable and shared adapters. Verify HTTPS, session revocation, deadlines, idempotent replay, and realtime reconnect in staging.

title: Initial configuration
description: Configure createGuildGate, production guards, and the 1.1.0 reliability boundary.
content: Initial configuration Production startup guards The production profile rejects non-HTTPS baseUrl, empty or wildcard origins, loopback/unspecified/mapped-loopback URLs, insecure session cookies, and weak secrets. Discord OAuth endpoints and callbacks must also use HTTPS. Session limit Official memory, Redis, and PostgreSQL stores enforce maximumSessionsPerUser inside session creation. A shared custom store should implement atomic create-and-evict through create(record, maximumSessionsPerUser). HTTP adapters return cookie-clearing metadata when they encounter an expired or revoked session. Reliability setting maximumLateSettlementMs bounds how long reservation and lease ownership may remain after the response deadline. Applications should pass context.signal to database and HTTP clients that support cancellation. Fail-closed audit An action in failClosedActions must enable audit and idempotency, require a transaction, and enlist the audit store in that transaction.

title: Installation
description: Add GuildGate 1.1.1 and verify its runtime and public export paths.
content: Installation Requirements - Node.js 22 or newer - A server-side TypeScript or JavaScript project with ESM support - A Discord OAuth application - HTTPS in production Fastify, Express, Hono, PostgreSQL, Redis, discord.js, and OpenTelemetry remain application choices: Published import paths Alongside the root package, these subpaths are published: Example: Do not import internal src/ or dist/ files. Semver applies to the root package and 15 public subpaths. CLI check Verify the version The expected value is 1.1.1. Continue with Start in five minutes.

title: Example projects
description: Use GuildGate 1.1.1 adapter, store, realtime, and test examples with correct boundaries.
content: Example projects The package examples/ directory contains small integrations. Adapt each example to your own authorization, storage, and deployment conditions. Adapters - Fastify: @kavtuai/guildgate/fastify - Express: @kavtuai/guildgate/express - Hono: @kavtuai/guildgate/hono - discord.js: @kavtuai/guildgate/discordjs An HTTP adapter establishes the response boundary; parsing, resource lookup, authorization, idempotency, transactions, and audit remain in the action definition. PostgreSQL and Redis Realtime and testing createRealtimeHub(), attachWebSocket(), attachSocketIo(), and createServerSentEventStream() share the same session and authorization kernel. A custom transport must call hub.acceptMessage() before handling a client message. Do not leave memory stores in production. Verify custom stores through runStoreContract() and driver-specific race tests.

title: Responsibility boundaries
description: Separate GuildGate guarantees from application and infrastructure responsibilities.
content: Responsibility boundaries GuildGate implements shared security and reliability mechanisms; it does not take over product-domain decisions. GuildGate boundary - Session token hashing, expiry, rotation, and revocation - Exact-origin and session-bound CSRF verification - Action lifecycle, deadlines, idempotency, and concurrency controls - Store, transaction, lock, realtime, and telemetry contracts - Stable user error codes with hidden server error details - Production startup guards Application responsibility Resource access, user/bot permission mapping, domain validation, schemas, migrations, retention, backups, Discord request budgets, proxy/TLS, and incident response remain in the application. JavaScript cannot forcibly stop an arbitrary promise. GuildGate returns at the deadline and supplies an AbortSignal, but the physical operation may finish later. A durable write that can outlive a lease should reject stale workers through fencing tokens. The transactional outbox provides at-least-once delivery. Consumers that apply external side effects must deduplicate by event ID.

title: guildgate-doctor
description: Run GuildGate configuration, store, analytics, and production checks from the CLI.
content: guildgate-doctor The doctor command inspects GuildGate settings and the project environment. It does not modify source files. Help Normal output Human-readable output shows each check and its status. Failed checks produce a non-zero process exit code, which CI should use. JSON output The JSON result can be retained as a deployment artifact or evaluated in a pipeline policy step. Review environment paths and configuration details before publishing it to public logs. Check areas Depending on the version and available files, doctor covers groups such as: - production URL and origin security - cookie and session bounds - store capabilities and adapter contract - transaction and audit configuration - Redis and PostgreSQL selection - realtime and analytics bounds - release and package metadata A successful doctor run does not by itself prove live PostgreSQL or Redis connectivity or application-specific Discord authorization. Run service-integration and application tests in CI as well. CI usage Run it after deployment environment variables are available. Do not pass secret values as command-line arguments. Troubleshooting 1. Fix the first failed check. 2. Verify production and staging environment files are not mixed. 3. Check the GuildGate version in package-lock.json. 4. For custom stores, inspect runStoreContract() results. 5. Run doctor again with the same environment.

title: guildgate-writing-check
description: Scan documentation for broken citations, temporary tool residue, and unfinished template fields.
content: guildgate-writing-check Writing check finds technical residue and unfinished template fields that should not be published. It does not decide whether prose is correct, well written, or authored by a particular person. Help Running the check Another project root: The command returns a non-zero exit code when a check fails. Issue classes it finds - unfinished or temporary template fields - broken citation markers - temporary identifiers from a tool session - file-upload placeholders - writing-block markers that do not belong in published content - large TODO fields left during copying This CLI page may name some markers to explain them; their presence in normal documentation is treated as an error. Issues it does not find The command does not replace: - verifying API names against source code - typechecking example code - opening and reviewing source links - evaluating translation equivalence - security or legal review CI Run it before the Docusaurus build. Fix the file and marker type reported by the command instead of adding a broad ignore that hides the issue.

title: Audit, outbox, and telemetry
description: Operate commit boundaries, cursor paging, at-least-once delivery, and OpenTelemetry hooks together.
content: Audit, outbox, and telemetry Audit records what changed, the outbox carries committed events reliably, and telemetry exports request timing and failure context. They are not the same dataset and may use different retention policies. Audit event AuditEvent contains these main fields: - id and requestId - action name - actor type and optional user/session hash - resource - success, denied, or failed result - reason code and policy version - bounded changes and metadata - creation time Do not write tokens, cookies, authorization headers, client secrets, or full OAuth response objects to audit. Add application-specific fields to audit.redactKeys. Fail-closed audit An action in the fail-closed list requires: 1. Audit enabled on the action. 2. Idempotency enabled. 3. A required transaction. The audit store enlists in the same transaction as the domain write. The commit does not happen if the audit insert fails. For ordinary actions, a post-commit audit issue may be exposed through postCommitIssues. Audit paging AuditStore.listPage() uses an opaque cursor: The cursor follows (createdAt, id) ordering. Records with the same timestamp are separated consistently by ID. A malformed cursor is an input error. Transactional outbox Action definition: The outbox record is written in the domain transaction. A worker later claims the record and sends it through the publisher. Delivery is at least once. Publishers or consumers must deduplicate by event ID. In the general case, the external side effect and the local “published” marker cannot be perfectly atomic. Claim bounds In 1.1.0, worker batch size, lease duration, and concurrency are bounded. A worker cannot retain a record forever; another worker may claim it after lease expiry. Before storing a publisher error, apply: - secret redaction - line and length bounds - a stable error code OpenTelemetry hooks The package does not require a specific exporter or collector. Use noopTelemetry for tests or installations without telemetry. Recommended low-cardinality attributes: - action name - result code - HTTP status class - retry count - post-commit stage - store or backend type Do not use user ID, guild ID, or request ID as metric labels. Carry them only in controlled trace or log fields when needed. Retention - Audit: longer retention based on security and operational requirements - Outbox: short cleanup window after publication - Traces: sampling and observability-platform policy - Application logs: redaction and access control Retention cleanup must not break cursor traversal or active claim leases.

title: Locks, deadlines, retries, and circuit breakers
description: Use GuildGate 1.1.0 reliability controls with bounded reservations, leases, and late settlement.
content: Locks, deadlines, retries, and circuit breakers Reliability settings do not hide failures. They define when work may repeat and where it must stop. Distributed lease The action concurrency field limits concurrent writes to the same resource: When LockStore.acquireLease() is available, the kernel supplies a fencing token. A failed renewal is treated as lost ownership. Why fencing is required A worker may pause long enough for its lease to expire. A second worker can finish a write under a newer lease before the first worker resumes. If the domain table stores a fencing token and accepts only a greater token, the stale write is rejected. Deadline In 1.1.0, the timeout result is returned at the configured boundary even when the underlying promise ignores AbortSignal. The settlement promise on DeadlineExceededError reports how that work eventually finishes. Application code should still honor the signal: Late-settlement bound This value limits how long idempotency reservation and lease ownership may be retained after the HTTP deadline. Do not use an unbounded value. The idempotency TTL should be longer than the action deadline plus the late-settlement window. When late work commits, the result is stored for idempotent replay so a later identical request can receive it. Retry Keep the retryable error set narrow. Validation, authorization, revision conflict, and reservation loss should not be retried. Before enabling retries, answer: - Is the domain write under the same idempotency key? - Does the external API accept its own idempotency key? - Does this worker still own the lease? - Does the next attempt fit inside the total deadline? Circuit breaker While open, the breaker rejects a new call immediately. This prevents an unavailable dependency from creating an unbounded queue. Do not create breaker keys with unnecessary tenant- or endpoint-level cardinality. Cache stampede CacheManager can use a renewable lease for cache misses. A fallback loader may run while the lock is busy. Preserve the lease and fencing policy when writing the fallback result; do not start uncontrolled parallel refreshes for one key. Observability Measure: - timeout count and actual settlement duration - retry count - breaker state changes - lease acquire, renew, and release failures - reservation ownership loss - rejected stale fencing writes Return a stable error code to the client while retaining requestId and action name in server logs. Tests - an operation ignores the signal but the response returns at the deadline - a late commit is available through replay - ownership is released after maximumLateSettlementMs - an old reservation cannot complete a newer record - lease-renewal loss stops the action - SQL rejects a stale fencing token - the breaker performs a controlled call after reset

title: Memory and Redis stores
description: Use memory for local tests and the Redis ephemeral store bundle for multi-worker deployments with correct bounds.
content: Memory and Redis stores Memory and Redis may implement the same store contracts, but their durability and lifecycle differ. Memory store The memory bundle is intended for: - local development - unit tests - documentation examples - a single-process test harness Session, idempotency, audit, outbox, and policy records disappear when the process stops. They are not shared across workers. Redis ephemeral store bundle fromIoRedis() adapts an ioredis-compatible client to the same narrow interface. The Redis bundle is suitable for shared short-lived behavior: - sessions - OAuth state - rate limits - cache - idempotency reservations - distributed leases Use PostgreSQL or another durable store for persistent audit, outbox, and policy requirements. Prefix Separate applications and environments in the same Redis cluster: Changing the prefix makes existing sessions and idempotency records invisible. Account for migration or forced logout during deployment. Atomic cache retagging When a cache entry changes in 1.1.0, the adapter: 1. removes old tag memberships 2. writes the new entry 3. adds new tag memberships 4. applies bounded TTLs to tag indexes that cover the entry lifetime These steps are atomic. Otherwise, a key may remain in an old tag set or active entries may be missed during invalidation. Reservation and lease Idempotency-owner checks and lease release or renewal should use Lua compare-and-set operations. An unconditional DEL key can remove a newer owner's lease. A Redis connectivity failure during renewal should be treated as ownership loss. When the domain store verifies fencing tokens, it also rejects stale-worker writes. Session cap The Redis session store inserts the record and evicts excess per-user sessions atomically. Apply TTLs to session-index keys as well so orphaned sets do not accumulate. Cache stampede The cache manager uses renewable leases. When the lock is busy, a fallback loader result may be used while load stays bounded. The loader itself should follow the deadline and cancellation policy. Operations - verify the eviction policy does not unexpectedly remove security records - use TLS and ACLs - collect latency and timeout metrics - do not depend on keyspace notifications for correctness - test session and idempotency behavior under maxmemory pressure - separate production and staging prefixes

title: Store contracts
description: Implement GuildGate 1.1 store contracts for a custom backend with the required atomicity and ownership rules.
content: Store contracts GuildGate does not bind the application to an ORM. The application supplies the ten GuildGateStores contracts directly or through official adapters. Contract version adapterContractVersion is 1.1. Action and realtime contracts remain 1.0. A custom store should record the adapter contract it implements and run runStoreContract() in CI. Operations that require atomicity Store Required behavior --- --- OAuthStateStore.consume Read and remove in one operation RateLimitStore.hit Counter and window update are atomic SessionStore.create Insert and per-user cap are applied together IdempotencyStore.begin Key, hash, state, and reservation are decided together IdempotencyStore.complete/fail/renew Reservation-owner compare-and-set LockStore.release/renew Only the token owner may change the lease CacheStore.set/deleteByTags Entry and tag indexes remain consistent OutboxStore.claim The same record is not leased to two workers simultaneously Idempotency owner token reservationId owns an inflight record. A SQL update predicate should check reservation and state as well as the key: Zero affected rows means ownership was lost. Do not delete unconditionally by key. Session cap A shared store should insert the new session and evict the oldest excess sessions inside one serialized operation. A single-process memory store can do this directly; SQL can use a transaction or advisory lock, while Redis can use Lua or an equivalent atomic command. Audit cursor AuditStore.listPage() accepts an opaque cursor and returns . Stable ordering is: Do not expose the cursor internals or treat it as a client-editable offset. A malformed cursor should produce an input error. Outbox claim claim(limit, workerId, leaseMs) leases records in a bounded batch. When a worker crashes, the lease must expire so another worker can claim the record. Sanitize and bound publisher errors before storing them in markFailed. Error contract Store errors must not disclose secrets or raw driver objects. Separate retryable connectivity failures from invariant violations. Preserve the cause in server logs so the action kernel can map it to a stable GuildGate error code. Test areas - competing consume calls - different body hashes for the same idempotency key - reservation loss - lease renew and release ownership - concurrent logins under the session cap - cache retagging and stale-tag cleanup - complete traversal with audit cursors - outbox claim lease expiry

title: Persistent PostgreSQL records
description: Configure transactions, cursors, rate limits, and outbox behavior in the GuildGate 1.1.0 PostgreSQL adapter.
content: Persistent PostgreSQL records @kavtuai/guildgate/postgres provides the official store bundle and transaction adapter over one connection pool. Migration SQL Review SQL without opening a connection: Before production execution, review transaction behavior, lock time, indexes, and rollback planning. Give the application user only the schema privileges it needs. Transaction finality In 1.1.0, PostgreSQL COMMIT is separated from post-commit callbacks. After a successful COMMIT: - the domain write is final - a callback failure does not issue rollback - a callback failure does not repeat domain work - the issue is observable through TransactionPostCommitError or action metadata Nested transactions A new run() inside the same transaction context uses a savepoint: A nested error runs ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT. The inner scope cannot change isolation or read-only mode. Its afterCommit callbacks join the parent only after savepoint release. Rate limits The PostgreSQL rate-limit store takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock for each bucket. The first insert and later updates use the same serialized decision path, preventing two workers from accepting requests beyond the limit together. Idempotency The reservation ID is stored in the table. Complete, renew, and fail queries include reservation id and state='inflight' predicates. No affected row produces idempotency reservation lost. Audit paging Audit ordering is (created at DESC, id DESC). The opaque cursor contains those two values and becomes the predicate for the next query. Avoid offset pagination because concurrent inserts can cause skipped or repeated records. Outbox An outbox worker operates with: - bounded limit - worker identity - claim lease duration - bounded concurrency On success it calls markPublished; on failure it stores a sanitized, short error through markFailed. Delivery is at least once, so consumers must deduplicate by event ID. Sessions and credentials The per-user session cap is applied inside the store transaction. OAuth credentials are ciphertext; keep encryption keys in a separate secret system so a database backup alone cannot reveal tokens. Production settings - calculate connection-pool size with worker count - configure statement and lock timeouts - monitor slow queries and deadlocks - separate migration and runtime database users - plan retention and index maintenance for audit and outbox growth - practice restore procedures

title: Custom store adapter
description: Implement the GuildGate 1.1 contract on another database or ORM with correct atomic behavior.
content: Custom store adapter When the official PostgreSQL or Redis adapters are not used, GuildGateStores can be mapped to the application's data layer. The goal is not only to satisfy TypeScript signatures but also to preserve behavior under races. Starting approach 1. Inventory the ten GuildGateStores members. 2. Record atomicity and TTL requirements for every operation. 3. Choose transaction, compare-and-set, and lease primitives from the backend. 4. Run runStoreContract() for shared behavior. 5. Add multi-worker race tests. Prefer 1.1 behavior over compatibility fallback Several methods are optional: - SessionStore.create - IdempotencyStore.renew - LockStore.acquireLease - LockStore.renew - AuditStore.listPage - OutboxStore.claim They are optional so older stores still compile. A production custom store should implement them to provide the 1.1.0 reliability behavior. ORM boundary An ORM upsert does not always provide the compare-and-set guarantee you need. Inspect generated SQL. If idempotency completion lacks reservation and state predicates, an old worker can corrupt a newer record. TTL cleanup Separate these behaviors: - treat an expired record as invalid during reads - physically remove records through retention or cleanup A delayed cleanup job must not change security decisions; those must use the expiry value. Serialization Bound unknown fields such as audit changes, cache values, and idempotency responses. Reject or safely serialize circular objects, oversized payloads, and prototype-specific values before they reach the backend. Transaction participation For fail-closed audit and transactional outbox, a custom store must enlist in the action's transaction scope. Audit written on another connection is not atomic with the domain commit. Contract test setup Application-specific tests: - 50 concurrent rate-limit hits - concurrent session creation for one user - two lease owners at the expiry boundary - late completion after reservation TTL - audit records with the same timestamp at a cursor boundary - outbox worker crash and claim recovery - invalidation while a cache entry changes tags Versioning When publishing the store adapter separately, state its supported GuildGate adapter-contract version in package metadata and documentation. Do not mark it as 1.1 compatible before implementing the contract changes.

title: Realtime hub and transports
description: Run WebSocket, Socket.IO, and SSE connections under the same authorization, replay, and backpressure rules.
content: Realtime hub and transports createRealtimeHub() separates connection identity, session validation, channel subscriptions, and delivery limits from the transport. It does not start a WebSocket or Socket.IO server. Creating the hub Defaults are bounded; choose narrower values for the application's event size and connection profile when possible. Attach sequence When a connection is attached: 1. Origin is checked against the allowlist. 2. The session token is validated. 3. The connection is indexed by session hash. 4. A ready message is sent. Authentication failure closes the connection with 1008. Channel subscription Generate channel names on the server or validate them with a narrow parser. Control characters and excessive lengths are rejected. After asynchronous authorization completes, 1.1.0 rechecks that the connection is still active and has subscription capacity. Concurrent subscribe requests cannot bypass the limit. WebSocket WebSocket messages pass through hub.acceptMessage() first. Subscribe and unsubscribe are not applied before payload size, message rate, and JSON shape are validated. Socket.IO parity In 1.1.0, subscribe, unsubscribe, and heartbeat events use the same controls as WebSocket messages. Socket.IO acknowledgements, replay, and backpressure derived from transport writable state are supported. SSE createServerSentEventStream() uses a bounded event queue. When the writer reports backpressure, it waits for drain; when maximumBufferedEvents is exceeded, the stream closes. SSE has no inbound message channel. The application should authorize before opening the stream and periodically revalidate long-lived access. Sequence and replay createSequencedPublisher() generates per-channel sequences. A client can send its last sequence as afterSequence and receive a bounded replay from the event log. Limit replay size. When a cursor is too old, provide a full state snapshot or reload path. Session revocation hub.revokeSession(sessionIdHash) closes all connections for that session. In multi-worker deployments, replace MemorySessionRevocationBus with a shared pub/sub implementation. A failed revocation listener must not stop other listeners. 1.1.0 isolates listener failures. Backpressure and send failure If bufferedAmount exceeds the limit, the client closes with 1013. When the send promise fails, the connection record is removed so a broken connection does not remain in the hub. Operations checklist - origin and session are checked during handshake - channel authorization runs on the server - Socket.IO events pass through hub controls - connection lifetime and idle time are bounded - session is revalidated periodically - replay batches are bounded - slow clients are closed - hub.close() runs during shutdown

title: Introduction to GuildGate
description: Understand the role, security boundary, and application placement of GuildGate 1.1.1.
content: Introduction to GuildGate GuildGate provides a guarded action kernel and infrastructure contracts for Discord dashboard servers. It keeps sessions, exact-origin checks, CSRF, authorization, idempotency, transactions, cache, audit, realtime delivery, and operator actions in one server-side decision pipeline. These docs follow @kavtuai/guildgate@1.1.1. The package requires Node.js 22 or newer. What the library handles - Opaque session tokens, absolute expiry, idle expiry, rotation, and revocation - Discord OAuth state and encrypted credential storage contracts - Exact-origin and session-bound CSRF verification - Separate user and bot permission decisions - Rate limits, idempotency, optimistic revisions, and distributed leases - Transactions, post-commit callbacks, cache invalidation, audit, and outbox delivery - Authorized WebSocket, Socket.IO, and SSE subscriptions with sequence and replay - PostgreSQL, Redis, memory, and custom store contracts - Operator actions, analytics, status monitoring, and OpenTelemetry hooks What remains in the application GuildGate is not a dashboard UI, ORM, or Discord command system. Resource ownership, role policy, domain validation, database schema, Discord request budgets, retention, backups, and incident response remain application responsibilities. Stable reliability boundary A successful database commit is final. A cache, realtime, or observer callback failure after commit does not report the domain write as rolled back and does not rerun the operation. The PostgreSQL adapter uses savepoints for nested transactions. Idempotency records carry reservation ownership through reservationId. A stale worker cannot complete or delete a newer reservation. An action deadline returns at the configured boundary; a late idempotent operation is observed for a bounded settlement window and a committed result is stored for replay. Realtime transports share payload, rate, activity, subscription, and backpressure limits. Audit pagination uses an opaque (createdAt, id) cursor. Outbox delivery is at least once, so consumers that produce external side effects must deduplicate by event ID. Starting order 1. Installation 2. Start in five minutes 3. Initial configuration 4. Action layer 5. Production security checklist

title: action() operation definition
description: Define a GuildGate 1.1.1 dashboard write with validation, reliability, and commit rules.
content: action() operation definition gate.action() keeps the security and reliability decisions for a write in one object. The definition produces an immutable DefinedAction; execution is performed by gate.execute() or an HTTP adapter. Authentication and CSRF authentication may be required, optional, or none. When an action weakens the default guarded behavior, record the reason in route review. Use csrf: "required" for unsafe HTTP methods. Disable CSRF only for an endpoint without a browser session that is authenticated by another signature mechanism. parse and resource parse narrows unknown input into an application type. Validate lengths, enums, numeric ranges, and allowed fields here. resource makes it easier to reuse one verified identity for authorization, optimistic revision, audit, locking, and realtime channels. authorize Returning nothing means access is allowed. An explicit decision is easier to review: Do not narrow Discord permission values to JavaScript number; use BigInt or discord.js permission helpers. Idempotency reservation 1.1.0 creates a reservationId for every inflight record. A store must enforce these rules: - return the stored response when the same key and request hash completed - report a conflict when the same key has a different hash - do not start a second execution while an active reservation exists - compare the owner token during renew, complete, and fail When an action commits after its HTTP deadline, the kernel can complete the result under the same reservation and replay it to a later request. Concurrency and fencing ttlMs is the lease lifetime; renewEveryMs must be shorter. waitMs controls how long acquisition may wait. When the store supports acquireLease(), context.fencingToken is available. The database update should reject a token that is not newer than the stored token; do not rely only on lock ownership. Transaction hooks afterCommit runs after the domain write is final. A failure there does not roll back the commit and is not a reason to execute the action twice. Retry and circuit breaker Enable retries only for work that can safely repeat. If an external write is not idempotent, action-level idempotency alone does not make the third-party side effect safe. The circuit breaker temporarily stops calls after the configured failure threshold. Its name is derived from the action when one is not supplied. Cache, realtime, and audit cache.invalidateTags derives tags from the committed result. realtime.delivery: "outbox" queues events at the transaction boundary. Do not include secrets, tokens, or unnecessary full objects in audit changes. Result metadata The HTTP layer must process ActionExecutionResult.meta. In particular, preserve replacement cookies, cookie-clearing instructions, and postCommitIssues. Use action test guild.settings.update in the console to inspect the control order.

title: Framework adapters
description: Bind Fastify, Express, and Hono requests to a GuildGate action envelope safely.
content: Framework adapters GuildGate HTTP adapters map a framework request into RequestEnvelope, translate the action result into an HTTP response, and apply session metadata to the response. Fastify Express Hono Proxy and IP information Supplying a trustworthy client IP depends on the application's proxy policy. Do not trust every X-Forwarded-For value directly. Configure which proxy is trusted at the Cloudflare, Nginx, or load-balancer boundary. Origin and cookies An adapter must process these metadata fields: - replacementSessionToken - replacementCsrfToken - clearSessionCookie In 1.1.0, expired or revoked sessions carry cookie-clearing information through Fastify, Express, and Hono responses. Preserve the same behavior in a custom adapter. Input merging When combining route parameters, query, and body fields, define precedence explicitly. Do not let the body override a security-sensitive route identity. Because guildId is assigned last, a body value cannot replace the route identity. Error response Send the stable code and localized message from ActionExecutionResult.error. Do not expose stack traces, SQL text, Discord tokens, or internal exception objects. Preserve requestId for logs and support records. Custom adapter checks Test these properties for a new framework adapter: - method and path are mapped correctly - multi-value origin, cookie, and header values are narrowed safely - abort signal follows connection closure - replacement and clearing cookie metadata is applied - an error status is not written twice - the domain action is not called again after the response finishes

title: Authorization and resource boundary
description: Verify Discord guild access, bot permissions, owner policy, and resource identity at the action boundary.
headings: Resolve the resource on the server
content: Authorization and resource boundary Authentication identifies the user; authorization decides which guild or resource they may change. GuildGate leaves that decision to the application during action execution. Resolve the resource on the server A guildId from route parameters or the request body is only a candidate. Verify on the server that the user belongs to the Discord guild and holds the required permission. Never treat client-provided isAdmin, owner, role, or permission fields as an authority source. Separate user and bot permissions An action may have two distinct requirements: - the user may change the setting - the bot may perform the Discord operation Even when the user is authorized, do not start an operation when the bot role is below the target role. Evaluate Discord permission bits as BigInt. Refresh authorization at write time The guild list collected during OAuth may be cached for fast UI rendering, but the security decision should use current data at action time. When caching access data, use a short TTL, explicit invalidation, and permission-loss tests. Owner policy The configured owners may change maintenance state or write block policies. An owner still: - passes origin checks - satisfies session and CSRF requirements - is rate limited - creates audit records Owner status does not automatically inherit another user's normal action permissions. When such behavior is required, add an explicit and auditable rule to the action. Maintenance and blocks A block subject may be user, guild, or ip. Hash or narrow IP data according to the audit and logging policy; avoid retaining unnecessary raw personal data. Permission loss and realtime Channel access is checked when a realtime subscription is opened. Revalidate session and channel access periodically for long-lived connections. Broadcast session revocation across workers and close matching connections. Test matrix Test at least these cases for every guarded action: - no session - expired session - invalid origin or CSRF - user is not a guild member - insufficient user permission - insufficient bot permission - permission removed immediately before the write - maintenance mode or active block - owner and normal-user paths

title: Writing standard
description: Maintain concise, source-backed, bilingual GuildGate documentation.
content: Writing standard GuildGate documentation must describe behavior that can be traced to source code, tests, or a published interface. - Keep public API names, error codes, and contract constants unchanged. - Separate the current stable release from historical migration examples. - State security boundaries precisely; do not turn a tested control into an absolute guarantee. - Keep English and Turkish pages technically equivalent. - Run code samples against published export paths and never include real credentials. - Release notes cover user-visible behavior, compatibility, migrations, and verified results only. - When a claim cannot be verified, narrow it or mark the remaining manual check.

title: CSRF and origin checks
description: Configure exact-origin allowlists, session-bound CSRF, and production URL guards.
content: CSRF and origin checks Origin checks and CSRF protect different parts of the same boundary. Origin limits which web source may send the request; the CSRF token proves the request was prepared for the active session. Exact-origin allowlist An origin is normalized by protocol, hostname, and port. The path is not part of it. Do not use wildcards, substring matching, or endsWith() checks. These are different origins: - https://dashboard.example.com - https://dashboard.example.com:8443 - http://dashboard.example.com Production URL validation In 1.1.0, production configuration rejects: - application URLs and origins without HTTPS - localhost and .localhost - 127.0.0.0/8 - 0.0.0.0 - :: and ::1 - IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses that resolve to loopback The same guard applies to configured Discord OAuth authorize and token endpoints. This prevents a production token from being sent to a local endpoint after an environment-variable mistake. CSRF secret csrfSecret must contain at least 32 bytes. Tokens are HMAC values derived from the session ID hash and a random nonce. Do not place the secret in source control. Plan rotation because replacing a single key invalidates existing CSRF tokens. Unsafe methods POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE are unsafe. They require a session-bound token unless the action explicitly sets csrf: "disabled". Do not modify data from a GET route. Cache and crawler behavior would otherwise create a write outside CSRF protection. Header and cookie layout Example client request: Do not store the same CSRF value inside the session cookie. Keep the cookie HttpOnly and provide the token through a controlled bootstrap endpoint or HTML payload. Proxy note Origin validation should use the actual Origin header rather than Host, X-Forwarded-Host, or referrer. Verify that the reverse proxy preserves it and redirects HTTP to HTTPS correctly. Tests - allowed production origin - same host with a different port - http versus https - missing origin header - malformed URL - CSRF token from another session - stale rotation token - safe versus unsafe methods - loopback and IPv4-mapped loopback configuration

title: Discord OAuth
description: Set up Discord OAuth with single-use state, encrypted credentials, and distributed refresh single-flight.
content: Discord OAuth GuildGate OAuth helpers control state consumption, credential encryption, and token-refresh races on the server. Redirect routing and user-profile mapping remain in the application. Authorization state Before redirecting, create random state, write its hash to the store, and associate it with a browser nonce. A state record may contain: - stateHash - a safe returnTo path - locale - creation and expiry times - limited metadata Use OAuthStateStore.consume() in the callback. Separate get and delete operations are vulnerable to replay races. Return URL boundary Do not accept returnTo as an arbitrary external URL. Use only an application-relative path or a server-side allowlist. Reject protocol-relative values such as //evil.example. Credential encryption Access and refresh tokens are stored as ciphertext in OAuthCredentialRecord. A key ring should provide: - one active write key - old keys that can read existing records - a key identifier or version Tokens, client secrets, and authorization headers must not enter audit events. Distributed refresh single-flight In 1.1.0, Discord token refresh uses the shared lock store: 1. Read the credential. 2. If refresh is needed, acquire a lease for the user/provider key. 3. Read the credential again after acquiring the lease. 4. If another worker already refreshed it, reuse the new token. 5. Otherwise call the Discord token endpoint and update the record. The second read prevents a waiting worker from reusing the same refresh token. For long network calls, a custom lock store should support renewal. Stop the credential write if lease ownership is lost. Production endpoint guard When Discord authorize or token endpoints are configurable, production requires HTTPS and a public host. Loopback, unspecified, and IPv4-mapped loopback targets are rejected. Failure behavior - invalid or consumed state: do not create a session - Discord invalid grant: mark the credential unusable and require login again - network timeout: apply bounded retry - refresh lease unavailable: wait briefly or reread the credential - decryption failure: record a security event without exposing secret details Scope policy Request only the Discord scopes the dashboard needs. Most guild dashboards use identify and guilds. Do not mix bot installation scopes with user OAuth scopes without a reason. Callback checklist - state is consumed in one operation - nonce or session association is verified - return path is allowed - token endpoint is called only by the server - credentials are encrypted at rest - refresh is single-flight across workers - the per-user session cap is applied after login - no token or secret appears in an error response or log

title: Sessions
description: Implement opaque session tokens, rotation, atomic per-user caps, and revocation with GuildGate 1.1.0.
content: Sessions GuildGate sends an opaque session token to the browser and stores only its hash. The CSRF token is bound to the same session identity. Creating a session The result contains: - session: the record written to the store - sessionToken: the opaque value sent only to the client - csrfToken: the token used by state-changing requests - setCookie: the secure cookie header Time limits security.session contains four bounds: - ttlMs: absolute expiry - idleTimeoutMs: expiry after inactivity - rotateAfterMs: token rotation point - maximumSessionsPerUser: active-session cap for one user Do not rely only on cookie expiry; validate the store record. Atomic per-user cap In 1.1.0, the official memory, Redis, and PostgreSQL stores insert a session and evict excess sessions inside one store operation. Implement this signature for a shared custom store: Calling listByUser() followed by separate delete() operations creates a race in multi-instance deployments. The kernel keeps a compatibility path when create() is absent, but an atomic implementation is preferred for production stores. Rotation When the session reaches its rotation threshold, action metadata may contain replacement session and CSRF tokens. The HTTP adapter must write the replacement cookie and the client must use the new CSRF value. Do not log the old token or persist it in frontend state. The session cookie should be HttpOnly. Revocation Revoking all sessions for a user is useful after account-security events, owner intervention, or OAuth credential changes. Use a revocation bus for realtime transports so open connections for the same user close across workers. Cookie configuration The production default uses Host-guildgate.sid. A Host- cookie requires: - Secure - Path=/ - no domain attribute SameSite may be Lax or Strict. Test the OAuth return and application routes before selecting it. Clearing an expired cookie In 1.1.0, an invalid session resolution adds clearSessionCookie metadata. The official Fastify, Express, and Hono adapters send a cookie with Max-Age=0. A custom adapter that ignores this metadata causes the browser to keep sending an invalid cookie on every request. Production checks - Is the session token transported only over HTTPS? - Does the store contain any raw token? - Is the Redis or PostgreSQL session cap atomic? - Is a rotation result written to the correct cookie? - Do logout, owner revocation, and expiry close realtime connections? - Does audit use sessionIdHash rather than the token?

title: Architecture overview
description: Understand the action, store, transaction, realtime, and observability layers in GuildGate 1.1.0.
content: Architecture overview GuildGate centralizes security decisions and write operations for a Discord dashboard server. It does not render a UI, own application data, or require a specific HTTP framework. Kernel createGuildGate() validates configuration at startup and creates these surfaces: - gate.action() for guarded operation definitions - gate.execute() for request execution - gate.sessions for session management - gate.cache for tag-based caching - gate.owner for maintenance and block policies - gate.revokeSession() and gate.revokeUserSessions() for revocation The kernel applies origin, session, CSRF, policy, rate limit, idempotency, lock, transaction, audit, and realtime decisions under one request ID. Action layer An action combines these parts in one definition: 1. Parse input 2. Resolve the resource 3. Check identity and CSRF 4. Authorize access 5. Apply rate limits and idempotency 6. Check optimistic revision and acquire a distributed lock 7. Perform the domain write in a transaction 8. Process cache, realtime, and audit results after commit In 1.1.0, an action returns at its configured deadline even when the underlying operation ignores AbortSignal. Reservation and lease ownership for a late idempotent result are retained only for a configured bounded period. Store layer GuildGateStores consists of ten small contracts: Member Responsibility --- --- sessions Session lifecycle and per-user cap oauthStates Single-use OAuth state consumption credentials Encrypted OAuth credentials rateLimits Atomic counters and windows cache TTL, stale windows, and tag invalidation idempotency Reservation ownership and replay results locks Leases, renewal, and fencing tokens audit Immutable events and cursor paging outbox Event delivery with claim leases policies Maintenance, blocks, and policy version composeStores() combines different backend bundles. For example, persistent records can live in PostgreSQL while short-lived counters and leases use Redis. Transaction layer TransactionAdapter lets a domain write and required audit or outbox records share one commit boundary. The PostgreSQL adapter uses savepoints for nested transactions. A callback failure after a successful COMMIT does not make the domain write look rolled back. The committed result remains final and the issue is exposed through TransactionPostCommitError or postCommitIssues in action metadata; the write is not repeated. Realtime layer createRealtimeHub() separates connection authorization and delivery limits from the transport. WebSocket and Socket.IO messages pass through the same payload, rate, subscription, activity, and backpressure controls. SSE output can use the same session and channel authorization model. Sequence and replay support lets clients resume after a disconnect. In multi-worker deployments, events can be claimed and delivered through the outbox. HTTP and Discord adapters The package publishes action handlers for Fastify, Express, and Hono. The discord.js adapter maps guild and permission data into the narrow interface expected by the kernel. The kernel does not own route structure, database schema, or the Discord client's lifecycle. Those decisions stay in the application. See the operation lifecycle for the detailed request order.

title: Operation lifecycle
description: Follow a GuildGate action from validation through commit and bounded late settlement.
content: Operation lifecycle The following sequence summarizes a guarded write executed by gate.execute(). 1. Request envelope The HTTP adapter maps the method, path, input, headers, and cookies into a RequestEnvelope. The kernel creates a request ID when one is not supplied and resolves the locale to tr or en. 2. Method, origin, and CSRF - The HTTP method is narrowed to the supported set. - Unsafe methods require an exact match against the allowed origin set. - A session-bound CSRF token is required unless the action sets csrf: "disabled". - Production configuration rejects non-HTTPS, loopback, unspecified, and IPv4-mapped loopback addresses at startup. 3. Session and policy The session token is hashed before the store lookup. An expired or revoked session adds clearSessionCookie to result metadata. Fastify, Express, and Hono adapters translate that metadata into a clearing cookie. Maintenance state, user/guild/IP blocks, and the owner set are evaluated in the same request context. Owner identity does not bypass the action security chain. 4. Input, resource, and authorization parse narrows raw input into the application type. resource creates the resource identity used by later audit and lock steps. authorize checks Discord access and application policy at the final write boundary. 5. Rate limit and idempotency The rate-limit store increments counters atomically. The PostgreSQL adapter serializes updates for the same bucket with a transaction-scoped advisory lock. For an idempotent action, the kernel creates a reservation ID. renew, complete, and fail apply only to the matching reservation owner. An old worker cannot complete or remove a newer record after its reservation expires. 6. Optimistic revision and lease optimistic.expected is compared with the current revision. A mismatch stops the request with revision conflict before the domain write. When concurrency is configured, the kernel acquires a distributed lease. If the store supports leases, a fencing token is added to the context and the lease is renewed while work continues. The durable write layer should reject stale fencing tokens. 7. Deadline, retry, and circuit breaker timeoutMs is more than a cancellation request. In 1.1.0, the response ends at the configured boundary and produces DeadlineExceededError. If the underlying promise settles later, its outcome is exposed through settlement. reliability.maximumLateSettlementMs bounds how long reservation and lease ownership may be held for that late result. When the physical operation must stop early, I/O inside execute must honor context.signal. Retries run only for configured retryable failures and within the same idempotency and lease boundary. An open circuit breaker prevents the domain call from starting. 8. Transaction and savepoint The transaction order is: 1. transaction.hooks.before 2. execute 3. transaction.hooks.beforeCommit 4. Required audit or outbox records 5. Database COMMIT 6. afterCommit callbacks Nested PostgreSQL work opens a SAVEPOINT. A successful inner scope forwards callbacks to the parent; an error rolls back only to that savepoint. The nested scope cannot change isolation or read-only mode. 9. Commit finality After a successful commit, the domain result is final. When cache invalidation, realtime publishing, or an observer callback fails: - the database is not rolled back - the domain write is not repeated - the issue is added to postCommitIssues or telemetry - the idempotent result is stored for replay Fail-closed audit can be enabled only when the action uses audit, idempotency, and a required transaction. The audit write must enlist in that same transaction. 10. Response metadata Both successful and failed results may include: - requestId - resolved locale - rate-limit state - replacement session and CSRF tokens - a cookie-clearing instruction - post-commit issues Do not drop this metadata in the adapter or application logging layer.

title: Threat model
description: Review the server-side threats GuildGate addresses, its assumptions, and responsibilities left to the application.
content: Threat model GuildGate is designed for controlled writes from an authenticated Discord dashboard user to a resource they are authorized to manage. The browser, client-side JavaScript, and every incoming request field are treated as untrusted. Addressed threats Threat Control --- --- Forged origin or CSRF Exact-origin allowlist and session-bound CSRF verification Stolen or stale session Hashed opaque token, idle/absolute expiry, rotation, revocation, and cookie clearing OAuth state replay Atomic single-use consume() Credential disclosure Application key-ring encryption and audit redaction Writes after permission loss Authorization repeated at action time Repeated request Idempotency reservation, request hash, and replay Concurrent update Optimistic revision, lease, and fencing token Old worker corrupting a new result Reservation-owner compare-and-set Rate-limit race Atomic store operation; advisory locks in PostgreSQL False rollback after commit Commit finality and a separate afterCommit failure path Realtime channel disclosure Session/channel authorization, periodic revalidation, and revocation Slow client or unbounded queue Payload, queue, buffered-byte, subscription, and connection-lifetime limits Duplicate outbox delivery At-least-once contract and consumer deduplication by event ID Local address in production HTTPS requirement and loopback/unspecified address rejection Trust boundaries GuildGate assumes these components are configured correctly: - TLS termination and proxy-header policy - secret management and key rotation - PostgreSQL and Redis access control - Discord OAuth application settings - correct route-to-action mapping - fencing and unique constraints for domain writes - logs, traces, and error monitoring Deliberately out of scope The package does not automatically solve: - XSS in the dashboard HTML or React application - operating-system protection for the Discord bot token - database backup and disaster recovery - third-party API availability - application-specific role hierarchy and business rules - malicious dependencies or compromised CI accounts Fail-open and fail-closed choices Not every dependency uses the same failure policy. Examples: - A write is denied when authorization cannot be resolved. - For an action in the fail-closed audit list, the transaction cannot commit if audit persistence fails. - If cache or realtime publishing fails after commit, the domain write remains successful; the issue goes to retry handling and telemetry. - Retry, timeout, and circuit-breaker bounds for Discord reads are selected per action. Review checklist When adding an action, answer these questions: 1. How is the resource identity parsed from untrusted input? 2. When and with which Discord data is authorization checked? 3. Can a repeated request safely return the same result? 4. Which worker wins when two workers write the same resource? 5. How is a failed post-commit side effect retried? 6. Does the audit event contain secrets or unnecessary personal data? 7. Does a realtime subscription close after permission loss? Keep those answers visible in the action definition, store contract, and tests.

title: Migration and versioning
description: Move from GuildGate 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 by updating custom store, transaction, and realtime contracts.
content: Migration and versioning GuildGate follows Semantic Versioning from 1.0.0. Version 1.1.0 is a minor release because it adds public adapter capabilities. Contract change Area 1.0.0 1.1.0 --- --- --- Adapter contract 1.0 1.1 Action contract 1.0 1.0 Realtime contract 1.0 1.0 When only official PostgreSQL and Redis bundles are used, the upgrade is more direct. Custom stores and adapters need the following behaviors. 1. Idempotency reservation Add reservationId to IdempotencyRecord. renew, complete, and fail must compare the same owner token. Remove unconditional updates and deletes by key. Return false when ownership is lost. 2. Atomic session cap Implement SessionStore.create(record, maximumSessionsPerUser) for shared stores. Session insertion and excess-record eviction must be one serialized operation. 3. Cursor audit Add AuditStore.listPage(). Apply opaque (createdAt DESC, id DESC) paging in the database query. 4. Transaction finality A callback failure after successful commit must not trigger rollback. Observe it with onPostCommitError or TransactionPostCommitError; do not repeat domain work. Use savepoints and callback-propagation rules for nested PostgreSQL transactions. 5. Deadlines and late settlement Return an action timeout at the configured boundary. Add settlement observation and the reliability.maximumLateSettlementMs bound. Increase idempotency TTLs to cover the deadline and late-settlement period. Forward AbortSignal to external I/O. 6. Fail-closed audit and rate limits Move fail-closed audit persistence into the domain transaction. Serialize PostgreSQL rate-limit bucket updates with advisory locks or an equivalent atomic path. 7. OAuth refresh Use a distributed lock for single-flight refresh and reread the credential after acquiring the lease. 8. Redis tag atomicity Update the cache entry, old and new tag memberships, and tag-index TTL in one Lua or equivalent operation. 9. Realtime transports Route Socket.IO subscribe, unsubscribe, and heartbeat events through hub.acceptMessage(). Add acknowledgements, replay, and transport backpressure behavior. Upgrade sequence 1. Create a separate branch. 2. Install @kavtuai/guildgate@1.1.0. 3. Fix TypeScript errors. 4. Implement adapter 1.1 rules in custom stores. 5. Run runStoreContract(). 6. Print and review PostgreSQL migration SQL. 7. Test login, guarded writes, timeouts, permission loss, session revocation, and realtime replay. 8. Make coverage and service-integration pipelines pass. 9. Observe audit, outbox, and late-settlement metrics in staging. 10. Perform a controlled production rollout. Rollback A code rollback is not the same as a database migration rollback. Verify that older code tolerates added columns. Wait for inflight idempotency records before removing reservation fields.

title: Errors and locales
description: Handle GuildGate error codes, HTTP statuses, retry metadata, and Turkish-English messages safely.
content: Errors and locales A GuildGate error result contains a stable code, user message, HTTP status, and retry information. Result shape details must contain only client-safe fields. Do not return SQL, stacks, tokens, or raw driver errors. Locale resolution The request locale is narrowed to a supported value; unsupported input falls back to the configured default. The package includes tr and en messages. An override key should match the stable error code. Keep code and display text separate; do not bind frontend logic to translated prose. Important 1.1 error areas - deadline and timeout - idempotency conflict - idempotency reservation loss - revision conflict - lock or lease acquisition - malformed audit cursor - origin or CSRF rejection - required, expired, or revoked session - maintenance or policy block - realtime subscription and message limits Use the installed version's errors.d.ts and runtime result for the complete code list. Retry decision retryable: true does not mean the client should retry immediately without bounds. A client should: - honor Retry-After or rate metadata - apply exponential backoff - preserve the same idempotency key - avoid retrying authorization failures that need user action Post-commit issues A successful result may include meta.postCommitIssues. This does not mean the domain write failed. The UI should show the committed state while the server handles cache, realtime, or audit retry paths. Request ID requestId may be displayed as a support code. Carry the same ID through application logs, traces, and audit records to connect the request chain. HTTP adapter Official adapters handle status and cookie metadata. A custom adapter must: - write status only once - preserve the error code - serialize the localized message safely - apply clearSessionCookie and replacement tokens - avoid exposing the server error cause

title: Public API
description: Find the GuildGate 1.1.0 core, adapter, realtime, testing, and operations export paths.
content: Public API This page summarizes the published surface of @kavtuai/guildgate@1.1.0. Use the installed package declarations and IDE completion for complete parameter and return types.
